summary: A 1940 CCC-built, roughly 100-foot steel tower near Forest, Mississippi, with outside stairs and an NRHP listing; no current condition or visitor report was found.

facts.design: Steel frame tower with stairs wrapped around the outside and a wooden hip-roofed cab (12 x 12 ft) with catwalk
facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Bienville National Forest (Bienville Ranger District cooperator)

events.note: Built by a local contractor working with a Civilian Conservation Corps crew. The NRHP nomination suggests it was designed for this site, which one lookout history site disputes.
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register, February 18, 1997
Added to the National Register of Historic Places, October 28, 1999

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Forest Lookouts site says the tower was formerly at the Shockaloo Tower site and was dismantled and re-erected in 1940. The NRHP nomination suggests the design was made for this site and does not mention a move. The sources conflict and the story does not settle it.

notes_for_editor: No 2024-2026 report on condition, climbing rules or closure was found after two searches. Access was left out because no source supports a level. Coordinates conflict: NHLR gives 32 19' 27 N, 89 30' 19 W (matches the brief); Wikipedia gives 32 24' 14 N, 89 28' 01 W, about 10 km away. The Wikipedia coordinates were not used. The NRHP form was prepared in 1998 by Todd Sanders and was signed by the Deputy SHPO on 10/27/98, with a site visit on September 27, 1997. The Shockaloo relocation claim comes from one lookout history site and is contradicted in part by the NRHP nomination. Unresolved.
